questions.a: B) Melting butter. Melted butter can set again; the other two make new materials.

questions.q: How can you get sugar back from sugar water?
questions.a: B) Evaporate the water. Sugar passes through a filter; evaporating leaves the sugar behind.
C) Frying an egg. Cooking an egg changes it into new materials; it cannot become runny again.
B) In salt water. Salt water speeds up rusting; dry air has no water.

questions.q: Testing temperature: what must stay the same?
questions.a: B) Amount of sugar. Only temperature changes; the sugar amount stays the same.

questions.q: Which jar shows rust needs water?
questions.a: B) Dry jar with rice. The dry jar had oxygen but no water, and did not rust.
B) Adolescent. Child, then adolescent, then adult.

questions.q: Which animal has the longest gestation in the table?
questions.a: C) Elephant. Elephant: about 95 weeks, almost two years.

questions.q: Which helps an elderly neighbour most?
questions.a: B) Carrying their shopping. Practical help with kindness meets their needs.
